gaps.before: persisted status='sent' + fabricated provider_message_id + logged 'Email envoye' + returned deliveryAccepted:true, with NO provider import or call
gaps.scenario: authed user 'sends' an HR email; DB row + mission log claim delivery on a date; recipient never received anything; evidence fabricated, no failed/unknown state exists
gaps.correction: fail-closed truthful: status='prepared', provider_message_id=null, log 'Email prepare (non envoye)', response sent:false / deliveryAccepted:false + disclosure

gaps.before: caller-supplied extra_values won over the DB canonical value for ANY canonical path; required_provenance enforced nowhere; contracts.ts spread fieldValues after the authoritative dates
gaps.scenario: HR user POSTs field_values forging employee.last_name / company.legal_name / employment.start_date / compensation.base_salary; rendered+hashed+approved+signed contract states a different person/employer/date/salary than the HR record
gaps.correction: DB wins for canonical paths (override rejected+traced in rejected_overrides); provenance-restricted client values rejected fail-closed; authoritative dates spread last in contracts.ts

gaps.before: normalizeDecision returned 'approve' for any unrecognized/empty decision string (model omits the arg, or 'attends'/'non'/'ne valide pas')
gaps.scenario: a decide_validation whose decision the model did not clearly express becomes an APPROVE proposal, so the human approval gate is satisfied by an unsafe default
gaps.correction: only explicit intents map; negation blocks approve; ambiguity -> null -> no proposal built (Pierre re-asks which of the three decisions)

gaps.before: prohibited patterns closed a truncated stem with trailing word-boundary (ASCII-only); matched 'licencie' (accented) but missed 'licencier'/'licenciement'/'licencie'; syndic missed 'syndicat'; handicap missed unaccented 'handicape'
gaps.scenario: protected-characteristic mentions ('syndicat','handicape') have NO structural backstop (analysis.ts has no discrimination rule) so the leaky regex was the sole net and leaked -> guard green -> autonomous execution
gaps.correction: accent-folded stem matching; word-boundary kept only where a stem would over-match a benign word ('virement'); all common inflections + protected characteristics now caught, 'virement' stays clean

gaps.before: clonechat_proposals has created_at but load() never read it and execute never checked age; a confirmed proposal was executable indefinitely
gaps.scenario: an old tab or a replayed proposalId re-authorizes an action weeks later after role/company/entitlement changed (violates section 4 EXPIRED approval -> AUTHORIZED)
gaps.correction: 15-min TTL derived from immutable created_at, fail-closed on unknown; expiresAt bound into the canonical command fingerprint; 410 PROPOSAL_EXPIRED with zero side effect (calls.length==0 proven)

gaps.before: finalizeVersion re-derived the content hash but never re-checked file cleanliness; createVersion enforced clean-file only at attach time
gaps.scenario: rescanFile() retro-quarantines a clean artifact after approval; finalizeVersion promoted it to final + document published + document.signature_ready on an infected file
gaps.correction: assertFileAttachable re-run at finalize; only the raw document lane leaked (the contract lane was already protected by contract-readiness artifact_clean, proven by test that 1 of 3 cases failed without the fix)

gaps.before: any terminal communication task rendered 'Envoye' with success tone; reminder/deadline_reminder succeed by SCHEDULING (external_side_effect:false), nothing sent
gaps.scenario: 'Relance Paul' -> action reminder -> succeeded -> cockpit shows 'Envoye' for a relance never sent
gaps.correction: schedule-only tasks -> 'Planifie' (neutral tone); v1.ts now consumes the canonical artifactStatusView presenter, removing the duplicate status brain that re-invented labels

gaps.before: 'Fais le necessaire pour Paul.' -> missing_info empty (only 'who'/'when' checked, never 'what'); the word 'Paul' silenced clarification; next='Executer'; invented a create_task
gaps.scenario: a vague delegation invents an action instead of asking which one
gaps.correction: explicit vague-directive detector -> request_missing_info, approval_required, no side effect; detection is on vacuity (not 'no operational rule matched') so clear instructions like 'Prepare l onboarding de Sarah lundi' still pass

gaps.before: an explicit user restriction ('...mais ne contacte personne sans mon accord') was ignored when the action was low-risk -> CloneGuard green -> autonomous execution
gaps.scenario: 'Notifier l equipe MAIS ne contacte personne sans mon accord' auto-executed; the 'Envoie le contrat...' case was safe only by accident because 'contrat' hits a sensitive rule, not the restriction
gaps.correction: strictest-wins: a detected restriction raises task sensitivity to restricted (CloneGuard red, prepare-only + confirm) and traces the conflict (user_restriction + prohibited_actions)

gaps.before: byHint ?? active[0] (cancel) and byHint ?? first-pending (validate): a hallucinated hintId fell back to an arbitrary target
gaps.scenario: 'annule la mission X' (X hallucinated) cancels the first active mission; 'approuve la validation Y' decides an arbitrary pending validation
gaps.correction: provided-but-unmatched id -> null (no retarget); no hint -> auto-pick only when exactly one candidate exists

gaps.before: client sent idempotency_key 'ui|<companyId>|<instruction>' with no actor; the server uses the client key when present
gaps.scenario: two users in one company, same instruction -> the second mission collapses into the first (user B receives user A's mission)
gaps.correction: client sends no default key; the server derives its actor-bound key [company,user,mission,instruction]; double-click still protected because the server key is deterministic

gaps.note: claimed: removeRole leaves the legacy pierre_rt_members.role, so ROLE_PERMISSIONS codeFallback perms persist after a role is revoked. Not fixed: needs a removeRole reproduction; changing the permission-aggregation model without a failing test risks broad authz regressions. Documented for follow-up.

claimed: a declared-but-empty field renders an em-dash in a final contract. Assessment: required-field emptiness is gated upstream (document-guard missing_fields and contract-readiness); an em-dash for OPTIONAL empties is a placeholder, not invented data. Making the compiler throw would break legitimate optional rendering. Not fixed without a repro that a REQUIRED field reaches the compiler empty AND passes readiness.

claimed: the executor runs before the CloneGuard black hard-block. Assessment: the only executor reached for sensitive/black actions is prepare_sensitive_draft (external_side_effect:false, decision_taken:false, no external effect); the guard black-check runs immediately after with no send in between. Low real risk. Documented, not changed.
claimed unauthenticated by default. REFUTED: both require the x-pierre-worker-secret header and return 401 otherwise.
